name: GNU Emacs
note: From the GNU Emacs Reference Card - parsed from etc/refcards/refcard.tex in the Emacs tree, the typeset source of the PDF the GNU project publishes, so every binding here is the card's own. Emacs notation is translated as the card's own "Key Binding Notation" section defines it: C-x is Ctrl+X, M-x is Alt+X, C-M-x is Ctrl+Alt+X and S-x is Shift+X; a multi-key binding such as C-x C-s becomes a sequence. RET is Enter, SPC is Space, TAB is Tab and DEL is the Backspace key (Emacs's backward delete). Shifted punctuation is written as Shift plus the unshifted key on a US layout, so M-% is Alt+Shift+5, M-< is Alt+Shift+, and C-@ is Ctrl+Shift+2. The card's section names are groupings rather than modes, so the context is empty except for Incremental Search, Query Replace, Info and The Minibuffer. The card's three-column tables (Motion, Killing and Deleting, Multiple Windows) become two actions each, named with the row's entity and the column heading in parentheses. Where the card gives an alternative binding on the same line the first is kept (C-x u for undo, C-@ for set mark, SPC for replace-and-go-on). Left out: the "Regular Expressions" section, which is regexp syntax rather than key bindings; every command the card writes as M-x followed by a command name (recover-session, revert-buffer, query-replace-regexp, the ispell and flyspell commands, the tags commands, shell, the input-method and coding-system listings, name-last-kbd-macro, insert-kbd-macro, eval-region, load-library and customize), which are typed command names rather than chords; and the four bindings that take an argument (M-z char, C-u num, C-q char, and selecting the nth menu item by number).
